en: The Therāpadāna,
Sobhitavagga 4:
The Apadāna of the Elder Pupphacchadaniya
“A brahmin named Sunanda by name,
a master of the mantras,
a reciter devoted to making offerings.”
Padumuttara, the knower of the world, the supreme and compassionate seer, caused the Vājapeyya sacrifice to be performed.
Out of compassion for the people,
the Fully Awakened One then walked back and forth in the sky; having thus paced, the Sambuddha—
The All-Knowing One, the Leader of the World,
suffused all beings with immeasurable loving-kindness, free from attachment.
Having plucked the flowers from their stalks,
the brahmin, who had mastered the mantras,
gathered all his disciples together.
He caused it to be tossed into the air;
for as far as the city extended,
there was then a canopy of flowers.
Through the power of the Buddha,
you have not perished for seven days; by that very root of merit, [you shall attain the goal].
Having experienced all success and having fully understood all taints,
he has crossed over attachment to the world.
In the eleventh century of eons,
there were thirty-five kṣatriyas named Ambaraṁsasana.
Universal monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Pupphacchadaniya recited these verses.
This is the fourth legend of the elder Pupphacchadaniya.
